# Neartect

> Neartect designs a microphone's near environment — walls, floors, niches, pipes, and gratings from centimetres to metres — and computes the filter it imposes on sound from a far direction or a point source, for one or several microphones. Browser app, no backend; the filter comes from a Rust core compiled to WebAssembly.

## Space document

A space is JSON with `kind: "neartect.space"`. Every field has a default; unknown fields are dropped and out-of-range values are clamped.

- `air.temperatureCelsius` — sets the speed of sound.
- `microphones[]` (1–8; a single `microphone` is also read) — `id`, `name`, `reference` (an object id the microphone is bound to, or null), `offset` — [across, gap, up] in metres in that object's frame from its anchor (a flat object's centre, a box's front face, a pipe's front mouth, a corner's corner, a recess's opening); a negative gap is behind or inside. `position` — [east, north, up] in metres (ENU), used when there is no reference. `pattern` — `omni`, `wide`, `cardioid`, `supercardioid`, `hypercardioid`, or `figure8`; `aim: { azimuthDegrees, elevationDegrees }` in the reference frame (the object's across, front, up when bound; east, north, up otherwise).
- `rigs[]` (up to 4) — `kind` (`xy`, `blumlein`, `ms`, `ortf`, `nos`, `ab`, `decca`, `binaural`), `name`, `reference`, `offset`, `position` as for a microphone, `aim` (the rig's front), `spacingMetres` (between the outer pair; a head's width), `angleDegrees` (between the outer pair's axes), and for `binaural` a `head`: `measured` (SADIE II KU100, fixed size) or `sphere` (Brown–Duda spherical head sized by `spacingMetres`).
- `source.kind` — `far` (a plane wave from `arrival`) or `point`; a point source has `reference`, `offset`, and `position` like a microphone, and `distance` (true: level falls with distance from a 1 m reference).
- `arrival.azimuthDegrees` (compass, toward the source), `arrival.elevationDegrees`.
- `render.sampleRateHz`, `render.lengthMilliseconds`, `render.order` (1–6).
- `render.quality: { reliefDetail (elements per shortest relief length, 1–24), elementLimit (most relief elements over all surfaces), movingDetail (0.1–1, the share of both used while relief moves or something is dragged) }`.
- `objects[]` — `kind` (`plane`, `disc`, `wall`, `grating`, `box`, `corner`, `recess`, `pipe`), `name`, `position` [e, n, u], `yawDegrees` (compass direction the front faces), `tiltDegrees` (0 upright, 90 front facing up), `size` [across, front, up] in metres (flat kinds use 0 for front; a pipe is [diameter, length, diameter] with its axis along front; a corner grows from its position along +across, +front, +up; a recess opens at its position and goes back by its depth), `material`, `strength` (1 physical), `relief: { shape: "flat" | "waves" | "arches" | "scallops" | "egg", heightMetres, periodMetres, directionDegrees (in the object's across–up plane, 0 along across), roughMetres (rms), grainMetres, offsetMetres, speedMetresPerSecond (moves the relief while previewing) }`. A `grating` has `pattern: { periodMetres: [across, up], barMetres: [across, up], thicknessMetres }`, a period of 0 leaving that axis without bars. A `wall` has `opening: { shape: "round" | "rectangle", sizeMetres: [w, h], offsetMetres: [across, up] }`.

The filter is normalised to the free field: with no surfaces it is a unit impulse at time zero. With several microphones the earliest has no delay, and the others keep their time and level differences.
